'''''Loreleia eucingulata''''' is an [[extinct]] species of [[coelacanth]] [[lobe-finned fish]] known from the [[Middle Triassic]] ([[Ladinian]] age) [[Calcaire à Cératites Formation]] of France. It is the [[Monotypic taxon|only species]] in the genus '''''Loreleia''''', known from a well-preserved, articulated skull and skeleton. Using [[X-ray microtomography|microCT scans]], an ossified [[lung]] was identified in this species and the closely related ''[[Graulia branchiodonta]]'', known from the same formation. This structure may have allowed it to transmit sound pressure from the lung to the inner ear.<ref name="Loreleia" />

== Discovery and naming ==

The ''Loreleia'' fossil material was discovered in outcrops of the Calcaire à Cératites Formation—part of the [[Muschelkalk]] assigned to the ''[[Ceratites|Ceratites praenodosus]]'' [[biozone]]—near [[Sarraltroff]] in [[Moselle (department)|Moselle]], France. The specimen is housed in the [[Natural History Museum of Geneva]], where it is permanently [[Accession number (cultural property)|accessioned]] as specimen MHNG-GEPI-V5789. The specimen consists of a nearly complete skeleton and skull preserved in anatomical articulation.<ref name="Loreleia" />

In 2026, Luigi Manuelli and colleagues [[Species description|described]] ''Loreleia eucingulata'' as a new genus and species of fossil coelacanth ([[Order (biology)|order]] [[Coelacanthiformes]]) based on these fossil remains, establishing MHNG-GEPI-V5789 as the [[holotype]] specimen. The [[Genus|generic name]], ''Loreleia'', alludes to the mythical figure Loreley in [[Lorraine]] folklore, the French region near the [[Type locality (biology)|type locality]]. The [[Specific name (zoology)|specific name]], ''eucingulata'', combines the [[Greek language|Greek]] prefix {{lang|grc|εὖ}} ({{lang|grc|eu-}}), meaning {{gloss|prominent}} or {{gloss|well}}, with the [[Latin]] word {{lang|la|cingulum}}, meaning {{gloss|belt}} or {{gloss|girdle}}, in references to the elongate [[pectoral girdle]] observed in this species.<ref name="Loreleia" />

To test the affinities and relationships of ''Loreleia'', Mannuelli and colleagues (2026) scored it in the [[phylogenetic]] matrix of Ferrante & Cavin (2025).<ref name="F&C2024" /> They recovered ''Loreleia'' alongside the coeval ''[[Graulia]]'' and the [[Early Triassic]] ''[[Dobrogeria]]'' of Romania, in an unresolved [[polytomy]] at the base of [[Latimeriidae]] (the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] containing the modern coelacanth genus, ''[[Latimeria]]''). The authors remarked that previous phylgoenetic work had identified ''Graulia'' as a member of the family [[Mawsoniidae]],<ref name="Graulia" /> which forms the [[sister group]] to Latimeriidae. They concluded that the precise relationships of the [[Basal (phylogenetics)|basalmost]] mawoniid and latimeriid taxa are not stable, and that ''Loreleia'', ''Graulia'', and ''Dobrogeria'' should be regarded as basal [[Latimerioidei]] ''[[incertae sedis]]'', pending more detailed analyses in the future.
